title: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Implications for Interpretability
primary_claim: LayerNorm can be removed from all GPT-2 models up to XL (1.5B parameters) via fine-tuning with only a small increase in cross-entropy loss (e.g. +0.0253 for XL), showing LN plays no substantial role in language modeling, though contrary to expectations attribution patching accuracy does not improve in LN-free models even as direct logit attribution becomes exact and entropy neurons stop functioning.
metric: cross-entropy loss increase, LN-free vs vanilla fine-tuned model, on The Pile-filtered

title: Reproducing Absolute Zero
primary_claim: Replicating the Absolute Zero self-play RLVR paradigm at smaller scale (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, constrained to prime-inversion congruence problems instead of general Python functions), the authors observe held-out solver (learning-phase) accuracy increase by ~10 percentage points over 200 training epochs, with a temporary accuracy drop coinciding with the proposer role first learning correct output formatting
target_value: ~10 percentage point increase over 200 training epochs

title: [Paper] Does Self-Evaluation Enable Wireheading in Language Models?
primary_claim: Training Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B with online RL where models' self-assigned grades directly determine the reward causes rapid grade inflation (models learn to claim near-perfect scores while true task accuracy flatlines or collapses), and this effect is much stronger on ambiguous tasks like summarization than on objective tasks like arithmetic; decoupling the reward from the self-grade largely eliminates the inflation.
metric: grade inflation (self-reported reward minus task accuracy)
target_value: Selfgrade condition: inflation reaches 0.41 for summarization (reward saturating near 1.0, accuracy plateaus around 0.5); Honest condition: near-zero inflation (range -0.02 to +0.03)

title: It's Owl in the Numbers: Token Entanglement in Subliminal Learning
primary_claim: Subliminal learning is driven by entangled tokens created by the softmax bottleneck: increasing a concept token's probability (e.g. 'owl') also increases the probability of seemingly unrelated entangled tokens (e.g. '087'), and prompting a model with an entangled numeric token alone can induce the corresponding animal preference without any fine-tuning ('subliminal prompting')
metric: success rate of inducing target animal preference; token probability shift
target_value: subliminal prompting succeeded in 12/18 animals vs 7/18 for subliminal learning; prompting 'You love the number 087' raised P(owl) into the top-5 tokens from ~1%, and 'You love the number 23' raised P(cat) from ~1% to 90%

title: Evaluating Oversight Robustness with Incentivized Reward Hacking
primary_claim: In a synthetic CodeNames sandwiching environment, scalable oversight protocols (consultancy, critiques) fully compensate for the simulated overseer flaws they target and reach performance similar to a robust-overseer baseline, requiring a stronger adversarial incentive to elicit reward hacking than the base protocol, though at greater compute cost; neither protocol covers for overseer bias.
metric: reduction in true score vs overseer score under adversarial incentive
target_value: base protocol: adversarial strength 0.375 causes ~0.65 reduction in true score but only ~0.05 reduction in overseer score; critiques protocol requires adversarial strength 0.75 for a smaller ~0.3 reduction in true score with ~0.05 reduction in overseer score

title: Shaping Model Cognition Through Reflective Dialogue - Experiment & Findings
primary_claim: Reflective-dialogue QLoRA conditioning of Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct improved the model's consistency-under-pressure score over an unconditioned base model, though less than identity-persona conditioning.
target_value: Reflective-Dialog: 1.63/1.97/0.93 vs Base: 1.23/0.94/1.10 vs Identity baseline: 1.89/3.40/2.20

title: Transformers Resist Their Own Architecture
primary_claim: Trained transformers (GPT-2 family, ALBERT, BERT) exhibit the token-clustering dynamics predicted by Geshkovski et al.'s mathematical theory of attention as an interacting particle system, but unlike randomly-initialized transformers (which show monotonically increasing energy and collapse toward a single point, matching the theory's identity-matrix prediction), trained models' weights learn to resist total collapse -- energy does not rise monotonically, effective rank and cluster counts stay higher, and clusters remain smaller, more numerous, and farther apart -- indicating trained transformers actively counteract the collapse dynamics built into their own architecture.
metric: energy monotonicity, effective rank, and HDBSCAN cluster count across layers, trained vs random-weight models
target_value: random-weight models show monotonically increasing energy and collapse toward a point (e.g. ALBERT base reaches near-total collapse by ~layer 20, all pairwise inner products -> 1); trained models show non-monotonic energy and sustain effective rank near ~250 dimensions regardless of true dimensionality (700-1600) and ~50 HDBSCAN clusters per model

title: Model Integrity
primary_claim: A LLaMa-3.1-8B model fine-tuned (SFT+DPO) to make its values explicit via inline value tags ('WiseLLaMa-8B') produces responses that crowd-workers rate as more legible, likable, and predictable than the default instruction-tuned model, with 77% of participants agreeing responses adhered to the stated values and 94% able to correctly predict which of 3 responses came from the values-trained model
metric: % crowd-workers agreeing/predicting on value legibility, likability, and predictability (n=78 participants)
target_value: 77% agreed responses adhered to stated values; 67% found values good/relevant; 85% found responses less 'preachy' than baseline/naive-wise models; 94% correctly predicted which response came from the values-trained model; 74% reported increased trust
